newsitem.title: USA: Deutsche sees no German bank mergers soon.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche sees no German bank mergers soon.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest commercial bank, said on Monday it did not expect any takeovers within the private German banking market in the near term.
"I do not see any takeovers within the very limited area of private banking in Germany in the near term," Deutsche Chief Executive Hilmar Kopper told a news conference here.

Referring to speculation that Deutsche's decision recently to take a small stake in Bayerische Vereinsbank AG was a first step to Deutsche taking a larger stake in the bank, Kopper said, "possibilities of mergers in Europe would be much more interesting than anything in Germany."
Kopper said he would welcome a change in legislation to allow cross-border European bank mergers, adding that this was not currently possible.

"Today this is not possible," he said. He added that any two European banks which wish to work together had to follow the route of one buying the other and then becoming a single bank run from one or the other country.
"This is a problem for the European business area," he said. "You cannot set up a company across national boundaries."
